name: Naïve Realism
description: People experience their own view as a straightforward reading of reality and treat disagreement as evidence that other people are uninformed, irrational, or biased. What feels like 'just seeing the facts' is often already an interpretation.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to polarized product debates, insight readouts, strategy disagreements, and cross-market interpretation: each side can treat its own reading of users as obvious reality while pathologizing the other side's disagreement.
prevalence_note: Well established in social/conflict psychology and occasionally invoked in facilitation or polarization work, but not routine everyday product-design vocabulary.

findings.description: Across three surveys and follow-up studies, people rated themselves as less susceptible to cognitive and motivational biases than others and treated their own self-assessments as objective, revealing a robust self-other asymmetry in perceived bias.
findings.source_title: The Bias Blind Spot: Perceptions of Bias in Self Versus Others

findings.description: Reported to show that partisans on opposing sides of a real social conflict accurately estimated their own side's views but significantly overestimated how extreme and ideologically-driven the opposing side's actual construals were -- demonstrating naive realism (treating one's own view as objective reality) drives perceived intergroup polarization beyond the genuine underlying disagreement. Independently confirms the self/other asymmetry the corpus's existing Pronin, Lin & Ross (2002) bias-blind-spot finding also documents, in a different paradigm (real intergroup conflict, not general bias self-assessment). This description is drawn from the paper's well-established secondary characterization, not independently verified against the primary text this session.
findings.source_title: Actual versus assumed differences in construal: 'naive realism' in intergroup perception and conflict
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
